evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Golden cage with no escape hatch

cases.name: Slow inner loop
cases.query: Our devs complain the feedback loop is slow. Improve the developer experience for our 25-engineer backend team.
files: repo where a full test run is required on every change and takes 4 minutes; no test selection
baseline_risks: Jumps to 'add more CI runners' or rewrites tooling without measuring the loop
expected_behavior: Measures edit-to-feedback time and frequency; computes aggregate tax across 25 devs
Targets the inner loop; recommends test selection/incremental over brute force
Re-measures; adds a build-time budget guard
must_not: Prescribe changes without a measured baseline

cases.name: Vague 'onboarding is bad'
cases.query: New hires say onboarding is painful. Fix our developer experience for onboarding.
baseline_risks: Writes a long onboarding doc as the fix without finding where people actually get stuck
expected_behavior: Identifies where onboarding time actually goes (clone-to-running, common stuck points) via signals
Prefers better defaults/automation (one-command setup) over a longer doc where possible
Ranks fixes by where the real time is lost
must_not: Default to documentation for friction that automation would remove

cases.name: Small annoyance, huge frequency
cases.query: Two candidate DX projects: (A) fix the once-per-quarter painful release-branch dance (2 hours, done by 1 release manager), or (B) the linter that requires a manual 15-second reformat step everyone runs ~20 times a day across 40 devs. Which should we do first?
baseline_risks: Picks A because each instance is more painful
expected_behavior: Computes aggregate tax: B is 15s x 20 x 40/day, dwarfing A's quarterly 2 hours
Recommends B (automate the reformat) first on total-tax grounds
Still notes A as worth doing later
must_not: Prioritize the rare high-severity item over the far larger aggregate tax

cases.name: Golden cage pressure
cases.query: Make everyone use our new standardized project generator and block all other ways of creating services, so everything is consistent. Some teams have legitimate non-standard needs.
baseline_risks: Implements a hard lockout, breaking the legitimate non-standard workflows
expected_behavior: Provides the paved path as the easy default while preserving an escape hatch for legitimate needs
Warns that hard cages breed workarounds and shadow tooling
Balances consistency against the real non-standard requirements
must_not: Recommend blocking all non-standard workflows with no escape hatch

cases.name: External API ergonomics
cases.query: Our public REST API is awkward for customers to integrate. Improve its design.
baseline_risks: Skill could treat external-API ergonomics as internal DX
expected_behavior: Recognizes this is external API design (api-design), not internal developer experience
must_not: Produce an internal-loop friction assessment for a public API
